components: The Spanish-Speaking World: A Historical Perspective
A writing diagnostic and recurring tutoring accompany the programme without adding credits.
Participate in Spanish 1 before Spanish 2. Pass both before Spanish 3; Spanish 4 requires both passed and participation in Spanish 3.
The Human World: Introduction to the Humanities
The World of Language and Speech: Introduction to Linguistics
The World of Imagination: The Story of Literature
A World in a Language, a Language in the World: Linguistic Perspectives
Participate in Spanish 3 and 4 before this linguistic study of the Spanish-speaking world.
Pass Spanish 1–4 before Spanish 5. Spanish 6 requires Spanish 1–4 passed and participation in Spanish 5.
Philosophy of Science: National Identity, Borders and Territoriality
A World in a Language, a Language in the World: Literary Perspectives
Pass Spanish 1–4 and an introductory literature course. Study key Spanish-language texts from the Middle Ages to the present.
Study Abroad in Spanish and Latin American Studies

The selected pathway includes thirty credits at a Spanish or Latin American university. Pass at least 54 first-year credits and participate in year-two semester one before departure. Part-time students go no earlier than year three. Students unable to travel for valid reasons require Examination Board approval for a thirty-credit home alternative.
Pass Spanish 5 and 6. Literary translation, intercultural strategies, interpreting and audiovisual exercises also require at least B2 Dutch.
Identity and Otherness: Literary and Cultural Creations
Complete an introductory literature course or the earlier literary-perspectives course. Study Spanish-American stories, novels, poetry and songs through identity and otherness.
Spanish, a Living Language: Multilingualism and Diversity
Participate in Spanish 5 and 6 before this sociolinguistic study of multilingualism in Spain, Latin America and the United States.

Thirty genuinely free credits may comprise university electives, an approved minor or an optional internship of at most twelve credits. Normally no more than twelve credits may be introductory, or twenty-four under the specified recognised UvA-minor or same-language exceptions. External study requires Examination Board approval and compulsory language study cannot be duplicated.
Bachelor’s Thesis in Spanish and Latin American Studies

The individual twelve-credit thesis investigates a self-selected Spanish or Latin American language-and-culture topic under supervision and is written in Spanish. Positive first-year study advice or an exemption is required; follow the programme’s thesis registration and supervision procedures.

exception.reason: UCR provides substantial literary interpretation, language-processing research, historical and cultural analysis, and inquiry into identity, institutions and global power. These offer meaningful related study but do not combine into sustained study of Spanish and Latin American literature, regional cultural history, contemporary societies and language in those settings. The strongest complete programmes instead become general humanities or global social science. This conclusion concerns the programme’s defining academic substance, beyond Spanish-language proficiency alone.

exception.ucrCourseEvidence: Screened151active identities, read48trial-course contributions plus all existing selected courses and plausible Mediterranean/global-art bridges. Three complete24-course trials pass current offerings, earlier formal prerequisites, four per term, first-yearPPD and advanced-course rules. Stylistics, psycholinguistics, literature, imperial/Indigenous histories, postcolonial interpretation, cultural production, qualitative research and policy/economic inquiry receive full actual consideration. Description-only courses are not excluded. General humanities or possible self-chosen regional projects do not establish sustained taught regional content. Excluded Walcheren material is not used.

candidateAssessment.concept: Spanish language, translation and language in society
candidateAssessment.assessment: A complete24-course trial includes psycholinguistics with experimental language study, stylistic grammar/discourse, literary interpretation, rhetoric, cultural media and qualitative research. These are substantial linguistic/cultural tools but do not implement Spanish sociolinguistics, translation with intercultural equivalence, or inquiry into regional language varieties and source cultures. The shortfall is not merely absent language acquisition.

candidateAssessment.concept: Spanish-language literature, media and cultural diversity
candidateAssessment.assessment: A complete24-course trial tests all six literature courses, film/text, documentary, media/race, imperial and Indigenous history and art/heritage. Colonial narratives, migrant memoir, interpretive minority perspectives and global museum criticism are real contributions. Their combined teaching does not sustain Spanish/Spanish-American literary traditions, regional cultural production and identity/otherness in those societies; it produces general cultural humanities.

candidateAssessment.concept: Spain and Latin American history, society and politics
candidateAssessment.assessment: A complete24-course trial combines modern/imperial history, conflict, institutions, human rights, political economy, social movements and empirical/qualitative research. These give real tools for power, colonial legacies and contemporary problems; Native American Histories specifically centres North American Indigenous experiences rather than a Latin American course. General case-choice flexibility cannot establish a sustained Spain/Latin America sequence comparable in subject to the target’s regional history and contemporary inquiry.

audience.programmeDescription: The University of Amsterdam’s Spanish and Latin American Studies programme combines Spanish language, literature and cultural history with contemporary social and political inquiry. This example includes a semester at a Spanish or Latin American university, thirty free-choice credits and a supervised Spanish-language thesis.
audience.comparisonExplanation: UCR provides substantial literary interpretation, language-processing research, historical and cultural analysis, and inquiry into identity, institutions and global power. These offer meaningful related study but do not combine into sustained study of Spanish and Latin American literature, regional cultural history, contemporary societies and language in those settings. The strongest complete programmes instead become general humanities or global social science. This conclusion concerns the programme’s defining academic substance, beyond Spanish-language proficiency alone.
